title: Free Gingival Graft and Collagen Matrix Revascularization in an Enoral Open Wound Situation
authors: Preidl RH, Reichert S, Coronel TV, Kesting M, Wehrhan F, Schmitt CM. J. Oral Maxillofac. Surg. 2021 Mai;79(5), 1027-1037. doi: 10.1016/j.joms.2020.12.019.
supports: Clinical study from the botiss mucoderm (porcine collagen soft-tissue matrix) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Authors' conclusion, verbatim: “The perfusion mainly progresses within the first postoperative week with only minimal further detectable alterations until the final investigation, comparable in both groups. Although integration of FGGs (revascularized) and the CM (new tissue formation) is biologically different, both transplants show comparable perfusion patterns, leading to sufficient KM. 32” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
